title: Finite primary module filtration for a p-group action
statement: Let ℓ be prime, Q an ℓ-group, and V a finite abelian group with ℤ-linear Q-action ρ and ℓ-primary underlying group. There exist n and a monotone chain F indexed by Fin(n+1) of additive subgroups, with F(0)=0 and F(n)=V, every F(i) Q-stable, and ℓ x and ρ(g)x-x in F(i) whenever x is in F(i+1).

source.place: Tag 0GIZ filtration assertion (proof omitted with augmentation-ideal hint); Tag 0GJ0 proof, finite monodromy and Sylow reduction. Agent-written fixed-point/Cauchy proof of the finite primary module case.

proof.text: Zero is attainable as the endpoint of a length-zero stable chain. The lattice of subgroups of finite V is finite, so Mathlib Finite.exists_le_maximal supplies a maximal attainable endpoint W.

If W is proper, apply [lem-sc-primary-invariant-extension] to get a strictly larger stable W′ with quotient trivial and killed by ℓ. Append W′ to the chain (using the old chain up to n and W′ thereafter). The new chain is monotone, stable, and satisfies the successor conditions, contradicting maximality.
Therefore the endpoint is V. Restrict the natural-number indexed chain to Fin(n+1); its successor conditions restrict to Fin(n). This includes V=0.

lean.statement: theorem exists_primary_filtration_of_isPGroup (Q : Type u) [Group Q] (ℓ : ℕ) (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (hQ : IsPGroup ℓ Q) (V : Type v) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℤ V] [Finite V] (ρ : Representation ℤ Q V) (hV : IsPGroup ℓ (Multiplicative V)) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (F : Fin (n + 1) → AddSubgroup V), Monotone F ∧ F 0 = ⊥ ∧ F (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧ (∀ (i : Fin (n + 1)) (g : Q) (x : V), x ∈ F i → ρ g x ∈ F i) ∧ (∀ (i : Fin n) (x : V), x ∈ F i.succ → ℓ • x ∈ F i.castSucc ∧ ∀ g : Q, ρ g x - x ∈ F i.castSucc)
